post.summary: Create a Design from a portable archive
post.description: Creates a Design from a zip that GET /artifacts/{artifactId}/versions/{versionId}/archive (or the app's source download) produced: send it as multipart/form-data with the zip in the field file (up to 26 MiB) and a JSON field metadata with the idempotencyKey. The zip's images and fonts are re-admitted as new assets of the new Design, so a Design can move to another workspace or account. The Design is stored as written by the tool in metadata.tool (default other), its build is queued, and source-quality findings come back as warnings. A zip with credential-shaped text, files named like AI tool or editor settings, unsupported or unsafe entries (path tricks, links, encrypted entries) or contents that do not match the archive's own inventory is refused with 400, as is a title or description with credential-shaped text. Refused source paths report agent_config_name, invalid_path or reserved_build_file. The whole body must arrive within 120 seconds (later: 408, reason upload_timeout, and the connection is closed). A person has one archive upload at a time and the server a few: another answers 503, reason upload_busy, with Retry-After. A move from an archive queues a build, so it spends a unit of the budget of Design pushes and checks per token and per workspace: when it is used up the answer is 429 with Retry-After, reason push_budget, before the body is read; when the budget cannot be read, 503 with reason budget_unavailable. Needs a token with the Designs permission.

post.summary: Check a folder without saving a version
post.description: A dry run of what a push or a create would store: the folder goes through the same rules as a push (paths, sizes, credential-shaped text, agent and editor setting names, packages) and then through a full build and render. Answers whether it builds, the findings with file, line and column, source-quality advice and the four screenshots of the default page. Nothing is saved: no Design, no version, no build, no stored image. Send JSON for text and already pinned assets, or multipart/form-data with the same JSON in a project field and repeated file parts for new images and fonts. Set each file part filename to its project-relative path. New files follow the direct upload path, type and size rules and must fit the asset budget with the pinned files. Multipart must arrive within 30 seconds or it answers 408. The JSON may weigh up to 10.5 MiB, like a push. Requests that exceed the transport size limits answer 413. A check takes the build service's one slot, so it counts like a push against the same budget before the body is parsed. When the budget is used up the answer is 429 with Retry-After and reason check_budget; when the build service is busy, being updated or too slow, or the budget cannot be read, the answer is 503 with its reason and retryAfterSeconds. A builder refusal of the source answers 400 with reason builder_rejected_source and a bounded message. Needs a token with the Designs permission.

post.description: Uploads one PNG, JPEG, WebP or WOFF2 file straight to a Design, so a push can name it in authoringManifest.assets. Send multipart/form-data with the file in the field file (up to 5 MiB; a Design holds 20 MiB of assets) and optional JSON in the field metadata. The type is read from the bytes: a file that is not what its type or name says is refused, and a too-large file answers 413. Sending the same bytes again with the same path choice, usage and altText answers with the asset already stored, even when the Design holds as many assets as it may. The whole body must arrive within 30 seconds (later: 408, reason upload_timeout, and the connection is closed). A person has one asset upload at a time and the server a few: another answers 503, reason upload_busy, with Retry-After. Needs a token with the Designs permission.

post.summary: Push a folder of files to a Design as one new version
post.description: Stores the files as one new version of the Design, on top of the version the tool pulled from, without spending Copera AI credits. Answers 201 with the new version and its build state; 200 when the push changes nothing or repeats a stored push; 409 with reason stale_head (and the changed paths) when the Design moved on, writer_busy (and retryAfterSeconds) while Copera AI is editing it, or idempotency_key_reused. When authoringManifest is omitted, new root HTML files and new nested index.html files become pages. The request body may weigh up to 10.5 MiB (a version holds at most 5 MiB of text, and JSON escapes can double it): an admitted request with a larger body answers 413. Pushes and checks share a budget per token and per workspace over a sliding window: when it is used up the answer is 429 with Retry-After, reason push_budget and scope token or workspace, before anything is stored; when the budget cannot be read the answer is 503 with reason budget_unavailable and Retry-After. The budget is charged before parsing the body, including on a push that later fails validation. Needs a token with the Designs permission.

idempotencyKey.description: Tied to the caller and to this Design: a retry with the same key and body answers with the stored version, a different body is refused

get.summary: Download a Design version as one portable file
get.description: Answers with a link, valid for 60 seconds, to the Design's portable zip: its source files, its pages and shared design, and its images and fonts. Issuing the link is logged and its stored zip is scheduled for deletion when the link expires. Send the zip to POST /artifacts/archives (here or in another workspace or account) to make a Design from it. A version that holds credential-shaped text is refused, as its source is, and files named like AI tool or editor settings are left out and listed in omittedPaths. get.summary: Get the build of a version, waiting for it if asked
get.description: Reads the build of one version without starting or changing anything: its state, the compiler findings with file, line and column, the failed files and resources, accessibility findings and a short-lived link to every screenshot per page and width. With wait (seconds, up to 60) it holds the request until the build has an answer (done is true) or the time is up, then returns the state it has. Links are made only for a ready build, once per answer, and work for ten minutes without the Authorization header. A request that waits counts against a small number of waits per caller: over it the answer is 429 with Retry-After, and a call without wait always works. Needs a token with the Designs permission.

post.summary: Restore an earlier version of a Design as a new version
post.description: Stores the source of an earlier version as a NEW version on top of the head: no version is removed. It answers like a push, so a tool handles both alike: 201 with the new version and its build state; 200 when the version asked for is already the head or the restore was already stored; 409 with reason stale_head (and what changed) when the Design moved on since baseVersionId, writer_busy (and retryAfterSeconds) while Copera AI is editing it, or idempotency_key_reused. A changeSummary that looks like a credential is refused with 400 and the field named in issues; invisible characters are removed. Needs edit rights on the Design and a token with the Designs permission.

expectedHeadRevision.description: headRevision of the Design when the tool last read it. The restore is refused with 409 stale_head when the Design moved on

idempotencyKey.description: Tied to the caller and to this Design: a retry with the same key and body answers with what was stored, a different body is refused

tool.description: The tool that made the change, shown in version history. Defaults to other

changeSummary.description: One line saying why, shown in version history. Longer text is cut to 160 characters
